lead_updates.title: Johann Friedrich Busse, Berlin clothmaker: weaving pattern book with notes in "a private cipher of digits and letter codes" (Stanford MSS Codex 1264)
lead_updates.date: c. 1768-1789 (title dated Berlin, 20 Oct 1772; addenda to 1893)
lead_updates.correspondents: Johann Friedrich Busse (no correspondent; own notes on orders and commissions)
lead_updates.shelfmark: Stanford University Libraries, Special Collections, MSS Codex 1264 (ArchiveGrid 1135494750)
lead_updates.why: A Berlin cloth maker's private trade notes on orders and commissions; the lead's 'military muster book' was a misreading of Muster-Buch.

seen.where: ArchiveGrid 1135494750 read in Chrome; Inlibris sale record bn49610 with leaf photos (title leaf, pattern leaf, dye recipe viewed)
seen.extent: 64 leaves in all; how much is cipher is not stated, and the cipher notes are not on the three dealer photos I opened
seen.cipher: Stanford's description, from the dealer: 'Interspersed are notes on orders and commissions, some written in a private cipher of digits and letter codes'. No decipherment is mentioned. The leaves I saw were clear German and pattern drafts; the ciphered notes themselves were not seen.

1903.unvetted: MNL record https://adatbazisokonline.mnl.gov.hu/adatbazis/a-karolyi-leveltar-rakoczi-kori-iratai/adatlap/10429 read in Chrome: no. 9027, Pongrácz János to Károlyi Sándor, Újvár 15 Sep 1710, 'titkos írás is', no image, no edition noted. BUT Commons prints from Révay, II. Rákóczi Ferenc és korának rejtjelezése (1974) a facsimile of a Pongrácz letter of the same day (caption: to Rákóczi, Kassa), and I saw its letter-by-letter interlinear decipherment (scan viewed in Chrome).
